To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PKC activation stimulates L-carnitie transport in rat astrocyte cells, and this stimulation is associated with an increased co-precipi-tation of Octn2 transporter with raft proteins, caveolin- 1 and flotilline-1, and with an increased presence of Octn2 at the cell surface, as well as with an augmented Octn-2 presence in cholesterol/ sphingolipid-enriched microdomains of plasma mem-brane.

1) Octn2 interacts with raft proteins, caveolin- 1 and flotilin-1 in astroglial cells, 2) this interaction is enhanced by PKC activation, and 3) the interaction with caveolin- 2, but not with flotillin- 1 is functionally relevant for Octn2 cell surface presence.
PKC regulates Octn2 trafficking to cell surface by increasing its association with caveolin- 1 in cholesterol/sphingo-lipid rich membrane microdomains (rafts) in rat astrocytoma cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the novel Octn2-interacting partner caveolin-1.
the role of PKC in Octn2 trafficking to cell surface and the involvement of caveolin-1 as a novel interacting partner of Octn2.
the molecular mechanism of Octn2 trafficking in astrocytes and its modulation by PKC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Octn2 is a PKC-regulated transporter, which is associated with caveolin- 1 in cholesterol- rich microdomains of plasma membranes.
PKC-dependent interaction between Octn2 and caveolin-1 is a novel mechanism regulating Octn2 trafficking and carnitine transport in rat astrocyte cells.
caveolin-1, a major structural protein of lipid rafts, regulates the cell surface expression of rOctn2 by PKC activation, which is a novel mechanism of Octn2 regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Octn2 is a PKC-regulated protein, that interacts with caveolin- 1 and is present in raft-like structures.
Octn2 is a novel interacting partner of caveolin-1.
Octn2 is a PKC substrate, which upon PKC activation interacts with caveolin- 1 and this interaction is important for its trafficking to the cell membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
caveolin-1, a key regulator of raft organization, can be a novel interacting partner of Octn2 and that PKC activation can affect Octn2 localization within the raft microenvironment.
PKC activation regulates Octn2 trafficking to cell surface and that caveolin-1 is a novel interacting partner of rOctn2.
PKC regulates Octn2 activity by controlling its presence in cholesterol/sphinolipid-rich rafts, where it interacts with caveolin-2.
